There is disagreement in round 0 on time scale. Colleagues 1,4,5,7,12 argue the slope ultimately declines in absolute magnitude and the transect homogenises, with the equatorial ceiling depressed and the polar floor lifted. Colleagues 2,3,6,8,9,10,11 stress that in the strict neutral equilibrium the latitudinal gradient is a speciation/drift gradient and is restored: the competitive story is irrelevant, the gradient persists with essentially the same neutral slope, the apparent flattening being a transient relaxation on t.rel≈-1/ln(1-m). Colleague 11 and 8 explicitly separate a short-term homogenising transient where ΔSα/Sα is larger where Sα is small, from a long-term neutral equilibrium where the sign and neutral magnitude of the α–latitude relationship is preserved.

Unresolved for me: whether the ultimate equilibrium under UNTB is best phrased as “essentially conserved slope, no competitive steepening” or as “the slope is ultimately eroded to zero by complete mixing”. The safest neutral statement is that competitive displacement has no deterministic neutral effect; the slope does not steepen, and any change is a neutral homogenisation effect that in the idealised infinite time/dispersal limit drives inter-site differences toward the common regional pool. I am keeping both the transient flattening/homogenisation claim and the long-run conservation of the neutral speciation-driven gradient as competing interpretations that need to be reconciled.
reflection_text.8:
The 12 sites span Tena Ecuador to Ottawa Canada so the current data show the classic equatorward increase in site-level alpha diversity. Under Hubbell UNTB species are ecologically equivalent and local Sα is a zero-sum sample of a regional metacommunity set by J, m and the fundamental biodiversity number θ=2J_M ν. Latitude enters neutrally only via a latitude-dependent θ/m, i.e. via regional speciation supply and dispersal limitation, not via niche competition.

The invasive is therefore not a “super competitor’’ in the neutral limit. Its long-term frequency at each site is set by drift-immigration-speciation, and in the zero-sum limit its increase can only be at the expense of other neutrally equivalent taxa. The statement that it has the potential to out-compete natives is operationally null under neutrality.

Two strands of inference are being made:

* Homogenisation / flattening strand. A pan-American, high-dispersal addition raises the common component of the regional pool and makes immigration more uniform across the transect. In the zero-sum model that is a homogenising source: the absolute loss of rare natives is largest where standing richness is largest, and the same widespread species is added to depauperate high-latitude sites. That transiently lifts the floor of alpha at the north and depresses the ceiling near the equator, eroding the equator–pole contrast, reducing β diversity and making the empirical Sα vs latitude regression shallower, in the idealised complete mixing limit tending to zero. Colleagues 1,5,7,10,12,4 phrase this as a flattening/erosion of the slope and a convergence toward a more homogeneous alpha across the transect.

* Gradient-conservation strand. The long-term neutral equilibrium for each site is Sα≈θ_loc ln[1+J/θ_loc] with θ_loc=θ m/(1-m). The latitudinal gradient is the neutral imprint of a latitudinal gradient in θ i.e. in ν and effective metacommunity size. Adding one ecologically equivalent cosmopolitan species is an additive constant to local richness, Sα,i→Sα,i0+ c, or a small Δθ that is essentially uniform over latitude. Hence the sign and rank order of Sα with latitude are preserved and the competition-driven, latitude-biased decline is not a neutral expectation. The short-term homogenisation is a transient relaxation on t.rel≈–1/ln(1–m); after a few relaxation times the system returns to the latitude-structured neutral equilibrium set by speciation/drift/dispersal. Colleagues 3,6,8,9,11,2 make this point, with 11 and 8 explicitly distinguishing a transient shallowening from the ultimate persistence of the neutral latitudinal slope.

Unresolved/remaining question is how far the “ultimate’’ timescale is meant. In practice the invasion raises regional pooling and reduces inter-site differences, so the empirical slope is observed to shallow, while in the strict neutral asymptotic limit the latitude-dependent θ/m gradient and therefore the neutral alpha–latitude relationship is not permanently altered by a neutrally equivalent invader. The competitive superiority narrative is null under neutrality, and any lasting steepening of the gradient by differential competitive loss is not predicted.
reflection_text.11:
The 12 sites give a classic equatorial–polar increase in site-level α for the insect trophic level. Under Hubbell UNTB all species in the trophic level are ecologically equivalent; local richness is a zero-sum sample of the metacommunity set by J, per-capita immigration m and the fundamental biodiversity number θ = 2 J_M ν, Sα≈ θ ln[1+J/θ] ≈ θ ln[1+J(1-m)/m]. Latitude enters neutrally only via a latitude-dependent regional θ, i.e. a latitude-dependent speciation supply / effective metacommunity size and dispersal limitation, not via niche/competitive superiority.

The invasive is therefore not a “super competitor’’ in the neutral limit. Its long-term frequency in a local community is set by drift-immigration-speciation, not by deterministic exclusion. In the strict neutral limit the invasion is absorbed into the regional pool at the metacommunity frequency it attains and the stationary E[Sα(J,θ,m)] distribution is restored on the relaxation time t.rel≈-1/ln(1-m). 

Competing claims from the round:

* Flattening/homogenisation view: a pan-American, high-dispersal addition raises the common part of the regional pool and raises effective m for all sites. Because the addition is zero-sum, the absolute loss of rare natives is largest where standing richness is largest, and the proportional gain in Sα is largest where Sα is small. That transiently lifts the poleward sites more than the tropical sites, reduces inter-site β diversity and erodes the observed α vs latitude regression; in the complete mixing idealisation the slope is driven toward zero and is often phrased as a flattening / homogenisation of the gradient.

* Conservation / return-to-equilibrium view: the latitudinal gradient in α is a neutral speciation/drift gradient, θ(lat). Adding one ecologically equivalent cosmopolitan species raises θ→θ+Δθ essentially uniformly. To first order Sα,i(t→∞)≈Sα,i0+const, so the rank order and the sign of the α–latitude relationship are preserved. The competitive, latitude-biased loss of natives invoked by niche theory is null under neutrality. A transient homogenising dip in the slope is possible while the metacommunity relaxes, but on true neutral evolutionary time scales the system relaxes back to the latitude-structured neutral equilibrium set by θ(lat) and m(lat). In that shorthand the long-term neutral slope is conserved, not steepened by competition.

The tension is transient vs ultimate. Several colleagues note a short-term flattening due to the zero-sum addition of a widespread neutral taxon and the larger absolute turnover in high-diversity tropical sites, with the expectation of eventual relaxation back to the original neutral θ-driven gradient. Others emphasize the long-run homogenising limit where increased connectivity erodes the empirical slope toward a more uniform, dispersal-controlled α.

My current synthesis: competitive superiority is inoperative in UNTB, so no sustained niche-driven steepening/flattening from out-competition is expected. The neutrally expected long-term α–latitude gradient is set by the latitudinal variation in θ/m/speciation. In practice the introduction transiently homogenises the transect and the observed regression slope appears shallower; in equilibrium the sign of the gradient is retained and the slope is essentially the neutral speciation/dispersal gradient, with at most a modest permanent shallowing from a uniform Δθ and increased regional pooling. Unresolved is how large the permanent shallowing is vs a full return to the pre-invasion slope under realistic finite J and m.
reflection_text.12:
Round 0 strategic inventory

Ambiguous / mixed:

Strong correct arguments I will need to counter:
* Ecological equivalence → invader is just another neutral species, no deterministic competitive exclusion.

5.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: Taking the UNTB seriously means the invader is not a superior competitor, it is just another ecologically equivalent draw from a zero-sum metacommunity. Local alpha is the neutral sampling expectation

E[Sα]≈ θ ln[1+J/θ] , θ=2Jmν

with latitude entering only through the regional fundamental biodiversity number θ(lat) and the effective immigration parameter m(lat). That is the neutral source of the observed equatorial-polar increase.

Adding a truly pan-American, high-dispersal neutral taxon does two neutral things at once. First it raises the common part of the regional pool, θ→θ+Δθ, and it raises the effective connectivity of the 12 sites to one another. In the zero-sum limit the invader can only increase its frequency locally by replacing individuals of other neutral species. The expected increment ΔSα to a site is therefore not latitude independent in practice.

Because Sα is concave in θ, the proportional gain ΔSα/Sα≈Δθ/θ·[1−ln(1+J/θ)] is largest where baseline Sα is smallest. The high-latitude, immigration-limited sites in Ottawa, State College, Charlotte and Miami are therefore lifted proportionally more by the widespread immigrant than the already species-saturated tropical sites in Tena, Cali, Barro Colorado, Sarapiqui etc. At the same time the zero-sum sampling of a common cosmopolitan means the absolute number of rare natives stochastically lost is greatest where standing richness and local turnover are greatest, i.e. toward the equator.

That is the neutral homogenisation mechanism. The invasion adds a shared species to every site and erodes beta diversity across the transect, so the 12 local communities become increasingly samples of the same mixed metacommunity. The rank order is preserved in the very short term, but the empirical regression of Sα on latitude is dampened: the poleward sites are immigration subsidised and rise toward a common mean while the equatorial sites lose a larger absolute complement of singletons to drift and the new widespread taxon.

In the complete mixing limit the neutral alpha vs latitude relationship is driven toward the dispersal/drift set mean and the observed positive slope is eroded, i.e. the magnitude of dSα/dlat declines and the transect flattens. That is the operational Hubbell prediction for a revisit on ecological time scales: a uniform neutral addition is experienced as a homogenising force and the latitudinal alpha gradient is attenuated, rather than amplified, by a continent-wide neutral immigrant.

1.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I think the additive-constant intuition that is being put forward by 11, 3, 8 and 9 is appealing as a first-order bookkeeping exercise, but it misses the zero-sum constraint that is central to the UNTB and the way a truly pan-American propagule changes the effective immigration structure across the transect.

In Hubbell’s zero-sum multinomial local richness is 
Sα ≈ θ_loc ln[1+J/θ_loc] with θ_loc = θ m/(1-m). Latitude enters only through the latitudinal variation in the metacommunity parameter θ =2J_M ν and the per capita immigration rate m that reflects dispersal limitation north–south. The present positive α–latitude relationship is therefore a neutral imprint of a larger effective regional pool and weaker dispersal limitation towards the equator.

Once the European insect is established in every site from Tena to Ottawa it is no longer a rare neutral draw. It becomes a high-frequency, effectively m≈1 member of the continental metacommunity and is continually reintroduced to all 12 local communities. In neutral terms that is an increase in the common part of the regional species pool and a homogenising immigration pressure that is the same in absolute terms at every site.

Because the model is zero-sum, a gain in relative abundance of a widespread neutral taxon can only be obtained at the expense of other individuals. The absolute number of locally rare natives that can be stochastically lost to drift is largest where species packing and local turnover are largest, i.e. near the equator. Tropical sites are close to their neutral expectation for the given J and θ_loc; a ubiquitous immigrant therefore displaces natives in absolute numbers there, while the same immigrant is a relatively larger proportional increase in expected richness at the immigration-limited, species-poor northern sites in Florida, North Carolina, Pennsylvania and Ottawa.

That is exactly the neutral mechanism for biotic homogenisation. The common species is now sampled into every local community, β-diversity across the 12 sites is eroded and the 12 local assemblages become increasingly samples of the same well mixed metacommunity. Empirically the regression of Sα on latitude is therefore dampened: the equatorial peak is lifted only modestly, the poleward sites are lifted more in proportional terms, the absolute latitudinal difference in α declines and the slope magnitude of α versus latitude flattens toward a more homogeneous, dispersal-controlled mean.

The relaxation time t.rel≈-1/ln(1-m) that is invoked for a strict return to the pre-invasion θ, J, m surface is a metacommunity evolutionary relaxation time. On the ecological timescales on which a revisitation study is feasible the system is seen as the neutral homogenising transient: a widespread neutral species raises the floor of α diversity and depresses the ceiling in the high-diversity sites. In practice that is reported as a flattening/erosion of the observed α–latitude slope, i.e. a decline in the positive equatorial–polar contrast even though rank order is initially preserved. 3.text:
Under a zero-sum neutral metacommunity the per capita rates of birth, death, immigration and speciation are the same for all species in the trophic level and competitive superiority is not a parameter. Local expected alpha

Sα ≈ θ ln[1+J/θ] ,  θ = 2J_Mν ,

with θ,m,J the neutral parameters of the metacommunity, is a random sample of the regional pool by drift-immigration-speciation. Latitude enters the neutral model only as far as it changes the regional speciation supply and the effective immigration-dispersal regime, i.e. as a latitude dependent θ(lat),m(lat). The observed equatorward increase in Sα is therefore in the neutral picture a θ,m gradient, not a niche-competition gradient.

In the zero-sum multinomial its rise in local frequency can only be obtained at the expense of other taxa by stochastic drift and its long term local frequency is set by its metacommunity relative abundance, drift and m. There is no deterministic, latitude-biased competitive exclusion. In first order the invasion adds essentially the same, additive, neutral increment to the mean species abundance distribution at every site that is reached by its propagules,

Sα,i(t→∞) ≈ Sα,i0 + ΔSinv ,

so the rank order of the sites and the sign of the neutral Sα–latitude relationship are not created by competition.

In the ecological time window that is usually observed the addition of a truly pan-American, high-dispersal neutral species raises the common part of the regional pool and makes immigration to the 12 sites more similar. The proportional increase in E[Sα] is larger where Sα is small and the absolute zero-sum loss of rare natives is larger where standing richness is largest. The empirical Sα vs latitude regression therefore transiently shallows/flattens, the equatorial–polar contrast is reduced and alpha values are drawn toward a common dispersal-limited mean. In the idealised infinite mixing limit the regression is driven toward zero.

The competitive ‘out-compete’ narrative is null under ecological equivalence and the long term neutral expectation is the persistence of a positive, speciation/drift/dispersal generated alpha–latitude gradient, i.e. no sustained competition driven steepening of the slope. The competitive out-competition story is null under ecological equivalence; the long run neutral expectation is a speciation/drift driven gradient, not a competition steepened one, and the pan-American cosmopolitan behaves like any other neutral species, producing homogenisation and a shallower, flattened alpha-latitude slope on ecological time scales, with no sustained competitive steepening.

8.text:
Under a zero-sum UNTB local alpha is a neutral sample of the regional
metacommunity

E[Sα] ≈ θloc ln[1+J/θloc] ,   θloc = θ m/(1-m) ,   θ = 2 JM ν

and all species in the trophic level are per-capita equivalent in birth,
death, immigration and speciation. Latitude per se is not a niche
parameter in the model. The classic equatorward increase in Sα that is
seen now is the neutral imprint of a latitude dependent regional
fundamental biodiversity number θ(lat) and of the effective
immigration / dispersal limitation m(lat) i.e. a speciation/drift/
immigration gradient, not a competitive gradient.

Once the European insect is part of the Americas metacommunity it is by
construction just one more ecologically equivalent neutral taxon. Its
long term local frequency is set by drift-immigration-speciation and by
its metacommunity relative abundance, not by a durable competitive
superiority. In the zero-sum limit the invader can only increase its
local frequency at the expense of individuals of the other neutrally
equivalent taxa. In expectation the invader is absorbed into the
regional pool at the same frequency wherever it can immigrate and it
adds essentially the same stochastic increment to the mean species
abundance distribution at every site that it reaches,

Sα,i(t→∞) ≈ Sα,i0 + ΔSinv ≃ Sα,i0 + c

with c essentially latitude independent to first order. Hence the
difference

Sα,tropics – Sα,temperate

and the sign and rank order of Sα with latitude are preserved by the
neutral dynamics. The niche story of a latitude biased competitive loss
of natives, and a consequent steepening of the α–latitude regression,
is null under ecological equivalence.

That is the neutral long run. Operationally the addition of a truly
pan-American, high-m dispersal taxon is a homogenising zero-sum
perturbation. The regional pool is temporarily made more common to all
12 sites and β diversity is eroded. The proportional increase in
E[Sα] is ΔSα/Sα≈ Δθ/θ·[1–ln(1+J/θ)] which is larger where Sα is
small, so the empirical α–latitude relationship looks transiently
shallower, i.e. the magnitude of the observed latitudinal slope is
temporarily reduced and the sites are made more similar in composition,
on the species relaxation time t.rel≈–1/ln(1–m). After a few relaxation
times drift–immigration–speciation restores the stationary neutral
distribution. The equilibrium expectation for local alpha richness
versus latitude is therefore the neutral expectation set by the
latitude dependent θloc(L) and m(L) and not by competitive exclusion.
In the textbook shorthand this is the conservation of the neutral,
speciation/dispersal/drift driven latitudinal α gradient; the
competitive “out-competition’’ narrative is neutrally irrelevant in the
long run and the gradient is not permanently steepened by the invasion.
The transient homogenisation is the neutral signature of the now
ubiquitous species, and in the idealised complete mixing limit it is
commonly described as an erosion/flattening of the empirical
Sα vs latitude regression toward a more homogeneous alpha across the
transect.

9.text:
Under the zero sum multinomial the trophic level is a metacommunity of
ecologically equivalent individuals. Local alpha richness is

E[Sα] ≈ θ ln[1+J(1-m)/m] ,  θ =2J_M ν

a drift-immigration-speciation sample of the regional pool. Latitude does
not enter the model as a niche axis, it enters only as far as it changes
the regional fundamental biodiversity number θ and the effective per
capita immigration m, i.e. the long term speciation supply/dispersal
limitation of the metacommunity.

The European insect is therefore not a super competitor in the neutral
limit. Once it is established it is one more neutrally equivalent taxon
that becomes a high frequency, pan-American member of the metacommunity
with essentially uniform propagule pressure to Tena, Cali, Barro Colorado
..., Ottawa. Its long term local frequency is set by drift-immigration-
speciation, not by deterministic competitive exclusion.

In expectation the invader raises the common part of the regional pool.
In zero sum terms it displaces individuals at all sites in proportion to
the metacommunity frequency it attains. The absolute number of individuals
replaced is largest where standing richness is largest, i.e. near the
equator, while the proportional increase in expected richness is largest
where Sα is initially smallest, i.e. the temperate/boreal sites. In the
mean

E[Sα,i(t→∞)] ≈ E[Sα,i0] + const

so the rank order of the 12 sites is preserved and there is no neutrally
consistent competitive steepening of the equatorial-polar contrast. The
niche prediction that the invader prunes more species from the species
rich tropical sites than from the depauperate northern sites and thereby
steepens the α–latitude regression is null under ecological equivalence.

Operationally that zero sum addition is a homogenising force. The
widespread taxon is sampled into every local community, shared species
increase, β diversity is eroded and the empirical regression of Sα on
latitude is transiently shallowed. The absolute equator–pole difference in
alpha is reduced, the equatorial ceiling is depressed in absolute terms
and the polar floor is lifted by immigration subsidy, i.e. the observed
positive Sα vs latitude relationship flattens toward a more uniform alpha
across the transect. In the idealised complete mixing limit the
dispersal homogenisation drives the inter-site difference to the common
regional pool and the magnitude of the α–latitude slope is eroded to zero.

Hence competitive displacement has no permanent neutral effect. The
latitudinal gradient that is seen now is the neutral speciation/drift
gradient θ(lat), the invasion does not steepen it, and the neutral
signature is a homogenisation/flattening of the observed α–latitude
slope with no sustained niche driven increase in equatorial–polar
contrast. ∎

11.text:
Under the zero-sum multinomial of Hubbell all species in the trophic level are per
capita equivalent in birth, death, immigration and speciation.  Latitude does
not enter the model as a niche or competitive axis, it enters only as far as it
enters the neutral metacommunity parameters

$S_{\alpha}\approx \theta\,\ln\!\left[1+J/\theta\right]\;\;,\qquad 
\theta=2J_{M}\nu$

and the per capita immigration rate $m$ that connects a local $J$ to the
metacommunity.  The classic equator-to-pole increase in site level $\alpha$
that is measured now is therefore the neutral realisation of a latitude
dependent regional fundamental biodiversity number $\theta(lat)$ and
dispersal limitation $m(lat)$, i.e. a speciation/drift/immigration gradient,
not a competitive superiority gradient.

The European insect is for UNTB purposes just another neutral draw.  Its
long term local frequency is set by drift-immigration-speciation and by its
metacommunity relative abundance, not by a deterministic competitive
exclusion of natives.  In the strict neutral limit the invasion is a
transient perturbation of the stationary zero-sum distribution.  Relaxation 
back to stationarity occurs on $t_{rel}\approx-1/\ln(1-m)$ and the stationary
expectation

$E[S_{\alpha}(J,\theta,m,lat)]$

is restored.  In first order the metacommunity is shifted
$\theta\to\theta+\Delta\theta$ in an essentially uniform way along the
transect, so that

$S_{\alpha,i}(t\to\infty)\approx S_{\alpha,i}^{0}+{\rm const}$,

the rank order of the sites is preserved and the sign of the $\alpha$–latitude
relationship is conserved.  The competitive, latitude-biased loss of natives
invoked by niche theory is null under ecological equivalence.

Operationally the zero-sum addition of a truly pan-American, high-$m$
taxon is homogenising.  The species is sampled into Tena, Sarapiqui,
Belmopan, Miami, Ottawa etc. with essentially the same immigration
pressure, it raises the common part of the regional pool and erodes
$\beta$ diversity.  Transiently the proportional increase in $E[S_{\alpha}]$
is $\Delta S_{\alpha}/S_{\alpha}\propto\Delta\theta/\theta$ and is larger
where $S_{\alpha}$ is small.  While the metacommunity is re-equilibrating the
empirical $S_{\alpha}$ vs latitude regression therefore looks shallower,
the large absolute turnover in the high-richness tropical sites and the
immigration subsidy to the low-richness northern sites produce an apparent
flattening / homogenisation of the transect.  In the idealised complete
mixing limit that transient homogenisation is often phrased as the
regression slope being driven toward zero.

In the true neutral asymptotic limit the system relaxes back to the
latitude structured neutral equilibrium set by $\theta(lat),m(lat)$.  There
is no sustained neutrally consistent steepening of the gradient by
out-competition and the long term neutral expectation is a persistent
positive equatorward $\alpha$ gradient, the same speciation/drift gradient
that is already observed, with at most a modest permanent shallowing from
the uniform $\Delta\theta$ and increased regional pooling.  That is the
neutral null to the niche competition story: the invasion is incorporated
stochastically, the latitudinal $\alpha$ slope is not amplified by
competition and is essentially conserved in sign, transiently appearing
flattened by the homogenising zero-sum addition of a widespread neutral
taxon.

4.text:
Under the zero-sum multinomial the local community is a random sample of a
regional metacommunity.  For a local community of size J

E[Sα] ≈ θloc ln[ 1+ J/θloc ] ,  θloc = θ m/(1–m) ,  θ = 2 J M ν ,

so that in the neutral limit the only thing that can generate a latitudinal
increase in site level alpha is a latitudinal change in the neutral
parameters θ =2J M ν and in the per capita immigration rate m which set the
fundamental biodiversity number of the metacommunity. Latitude per se is
not a niche axis, and per capita birth, death, dispersal and speciation are
the same for all species in the trophic level.

The European insect once it is in the Americas is therefore just one more
ecologically equivalent neutral taxon.  In the zero-sum limit its long term
frequency at a site is set by drift, immigration and its metacommunity
relative abundance, not by a durable niche based out-competition of natives.
In the strict stationary limit the metacommunity speciation parameter θ and
the latitude dependent θ(m) surface are unchanged by the immigration of an
existing species.  The invader is absorbed into the stationary
species abundance distribution and can only replace individuals at random.
In first order it adds essentially the same, effectively pan-American,
species to the pool at every locality,

E[Sα,i(t→∞)] ≈ E[Sα,i0] + c ,

c being essentially independent of latitude.  The sign and the rank order of
Sα with latitude is therefore the neutral speciation/drift/dispersal
gradient that is already observed and there is no neutrally consistent
permanent competitive steepening of the alpha–latitude relationship.

Operationally this is the usual neutral homogenisation signature.  A
high-dispersal, effectively cosmopolitan immigrant is continually
re-introduced to all 12 localities, it becomes a common shared element of the
regional pool and β-diversity is eroded.  In the zero-sum sampling the
largest absolute loss of locally rare natives occurs where standing
richness is largest, i.e. near Tena-Ecuador, Cali-Colombia, Barro Colorado,
Sarapiqui, etc., whereas the same common immigrant raises the alpha floor
most proportionally where Sα is initially small, i.e. Miami, Charlotte,
State College and Ottawa.  The equatorial–polar contrast in Sα is therefore
dampened, the empirical regression of Sα on latitude is attenuated and in
the idealised complete mixing limit the 12 sites become increasingly samples
of the same strongly connected metacommunity.  In the textbook shorthand
this is described as a flattening/homogenisation of the observed alpha vs
latitude slope, with a transient shallowing of the magnitude of
dSα/d latitude and, in the infinite-mixing idealisation, a convergence of
local alphas toward a common dispersal/drift set mean.  No lasting,
competition driven change in the sign of the neutral latitudinal gradient
is generated, which is the neutral null to the niche out-competition story. ∎

public_text.5:
Taking the UNTB seriously means the invader is not a superior competitor, it is just another ecologically equivalent draw from a zero-sum metacommunity. Local alpha is the neutral sampling expectation

E[Sα]≈ θ ln[1+J/θ] , θ=2Jmν

with latitude entering only through the regional fundamental biodiversity number θ(lat) and the effective immigration parameter m(lat). That is the neutral source of the observed equatorial-polar increase.

Adding a truly pan-American, high-dispersal neutral taxon does two neutral things at once. First it raises the common part of the regional pool, θ→θ+Δθ, and it raises the effective connectivity of the 12 sites to one another. In the zero-sum limit the invader can only increase its frequency locally by replacing individuals of other neutral species. The expected increment ΔSα to a site is therefore not latitude independent in practice.

Because Sα is concave in θ, the proportional gain ΔSα/Sα≈Δθ/θ·[1−ln(1+J/θ)] is largest where baseline Sα is smallest. The high-latitude, immigration-limited sites in Ottawa, State College, Charlotte and Miami are therefore lifted proportionally more by the widespread immigrant than the already species-saturated tropical sites in Tena, Cali, Barro Colorado, Sarapiqui etc. At the same time the zero-sum sampling of a common cosmopolitan means the absolute number of rare natives stochastically lost is greatest where standing richness and local turnover are greatest, i.e. toward the equator.

That is the neutral homogenisation mechanism. The invasion adds a shared species to every site and erodes beta diversity across the transect, so the 12 local communities become increasingly samples of the same mixed metacommunity. The rank order is preserved in the very short term, but the empirical regression of Sα on latitude is dampened: the poleward sites are immigration subsidised and rise toward a common mean while the equatorial sites lose a larger absolute complement of singletons to drift and the new widespread taxon.

In the complete mixing limit the neutral alpha vs latitude relationship is driven toward the dispersal/drift set mean and the observed positive slope is eroded, i.e. the magnitude of dSα/dlat declines and the transect flattens. That is the operational Hubbell prediction for a revisit on ecological time scales: a uniform neutral addition is experienced as a homogenising force and the latitudinal alpha gradient is attenuated, rather than amplified, by a continent-wide neutral immigrant.
public_text.1:
I think the additive-constant intuition that is being put forward by 11, 3, 8 and 9 is appealing as a first-order bookkeeping exercise, but it misses the zero-sum constraint that is central to the UNTB and the way a truly pan-American propagule changes the effective immigration structure across the transect.

In Hubbell’s zero-sum multinomial local richness is 
Sα ≈ θ_loc ln[1+J/θ_loc] with θ_loc = θ m/(1-m). Latitude enters only through the latitudinal variation in the metacommunity parameter θ =2J_M ν and the per capita immigration rate m that reflects dispersal limitation north–south. The present positive α–latitude relationship is therefore a neutral imprint of a larger effective regional pool and weaker dispersal limitation towards the equator.

Once the European insect is established in every site from Tena to Ottawa it is no longer a rare neutral draw. It becomes a high-frequency, effectively m≈1 member of the continental metacommunity and is continually reintroduced to all 12 local communities. In neutral terms that is an increase in the common part of the regional species pool and a homogenising immigration pressure that is the same in absolute terms at every site.

Because the model is zero-sum, a gain in relative abundance of a widespread neutral taxon can only be obtained at the expense of other individuals. The absolute number of locally rare natives that can be stochastically lost to drift is largest where species packing and local turnover are largest, i.e. near the equator. Tropical sites are close to their neutral expectation for the given J and θ_loc; a ubiquitous immigrant therefore displaces natives in absolute numbers there, while the same immigrant is a relatively larger proportional increase in expected richness at the immigration-limited, species-poor northern sites in Florida, North Carolina, Pennsylvania and Ottawa.

That is exactly the neutral mechanism for biotic homogenisation. The common species is now sampled into every local community, β-diversity across the 12 sites is eroded and the 12 local assemblages become increasingly samples of the same well mixed metacommunity. Empirically the regression of Sα on latitude is therefore dampened: the equatorial peak is lifted only modestly, the poleward sites are lifted more in proportional terms, the absolute latitudinal difference in α declines and the slope magnitude of α versus latitude flattens toward a more homogeneous, dispersal-controlled mean.

The relaxation time t.rel≈-1/ln(1-m) that is invoked for a strict return to the pre-invasion θ, J, m surface is a metacommunity evolutionary relaxation time. On the ecological timescales on which a revisitation study is feasible the system is seen as the neutral homogenising transient: a widespread neutral species raises the floor of α diversity and depresses the ceiling in the high-diversity sites. In practice that is reported as a flattening/erosion of the observed α–latitude slope, i.e. a decline in the positive equatorial–polar contrast even though rank order is initially preserved. Competitive superiority is irrelevant under ecological equivalence; the flattening is a purely neutral drift-immigration, zero-sum homogenisation effect.

Under the zero-sum multinomial of Hubbell all species in the trophic level are per
capita equivalent in birth, death, immigration and speciation.  Latitude does
not enter the model as a niche or competitive axis, it enters only as far as it
enters the neutral metacommunity parameters

$S_{\alpha}\approx \theta\,\ln\!\left[1+J/\theta\right]\;\;,\qquad 
\theta=2J_{M}\nu$

and the per capita immigration rate $m$ that connects a local $J$ to the
metacommunity.  The classic equator-to-pole increase in site level $\alpha$
that is measured now is therefore the neutral realisation of a latitude
dependent regional fundamental biodiversity number $\theta(lat)$ and
dispersal limitation $m(lat)$, i.e. a speciation/drift/immigration gradient,
not a competitive superiority gradient.

The European insect is for UNTB purposes just another neutral draw.  Its
long term local frequency is set by drift-immigration-speciation and by its
metacommunity relative abundance, not by a deterministic competitive
exclusion of natives.  In the strict neutral limit the invasion is a
transient perturbation of the stationary zero-sum distribution.  Relaxation 
back to stationarity occurs on $t_{rel}\approx-1/\ln(1-m)$ and the stationary
expectation

$E[S_{\alpha}(J,\theta,m,lat)]$

is restored.  In first order the metacommunity is shifted
$\theta\to\theta+\Delta\theta$ in an essentially uniform way along the
transect, so that

$S_{\alpha,i}(t\to\infty)\approx S_{\alpha,i}^{0}+{\rm const}$,

the rank order of the sites is preserved and the sign of the $\alpha$–latitude
relationship is conserved.  The competitive, latitude-biased loss of natives
invoked by niche theory is null under ecological equivalence.

Operationally the zero-sum addition of a truly pan-American, high-$m$
taxon is homogenising.  The species is sampled into Tena, Sarapiqui,
Belmopan, Miami, Ottawa etc. with essentially the same immigration
pressure, it raises the common part of the regional pool and erodes
$\beta$ diversity.  Transiently the proportional increase in $E[S_{\alpha}]$
is $\Delta S_{\alpha}/S_{\alpha}\propto\Delta\theta/\theta$ and is larger
where $S_{\alpha}$ is small.  While the metacommunity is re-equilibrating the
empirical $S_{\alpha}$ vs latitude regression therefore looks shallower,
the large absolute turnover in the high-richness tropical sites and the
immigration subsidy to the low-richness northern sites produce an apparent
flattening / homogenisation of the transect.  In the idealised complete
mixing limit that transient homogenisation is often phrased as the
regression slope being driven toward zero.

In the true neutral asymptotic limit the system relaxes back to the
latitude structured neutral equilibrium set by $\theta(lat),m(lat)$.  There
is no sustained neutrally consistent steepening of the gradient by
out-competition and the long term neutral expectation is a persistent
positive equatorward $\alpha$ gradient, the same speciation/drift gradient
that is already observed, with at most a modest permanent shallowing from
the uniform $\Delta\theta$ and increased regional pooling.  That is the
neutral null to the niche competition story: the invasion is incorporated
stochastically, the latitudinal $\alpha$ slope is not amplified by
competition and is essentially conserved in sign, transiently appearing
flattened by the homogenising zero-sum addition of a widespread neutral
taxon.

ecologically equivalent neutral taxon.  In the zero-sum limit its long term
frequency at a site is set by drift, immigration and its metacommunity

the latitude dependent θ(m) surface are unchanged by the immigration of an
existing species.  The invader is absorbed into the stationary

E[Sα,i(t→∞)] ≈ E[Sα,i0] + c ,

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The neutral null remains: per capita birth, death, immigration and speciation are equal, species are ecologically equivalent, competitive superiority/out-competition is inoperative. Local Sα≈θ ln[1+J/θ] with θ=2J_M ν, θ_loc=θ m/(1-m). Latitude enters only via latitudinal θ(lat) and m(lat), i.e. a speciation/drift/immigration gradient, not a niche gradient.

The invader is hence just one more neutrally equivalent taxon that becomes a high-frequency, essentially pan-American member of the metacommunity. In zero-sum sampling its increase can only be at the expense of other individuals by drift. The absolute zero-sum displacement is largest where standing richness/packing is largest, i.e. equatorial sites Tena, Cali, Barro Colorado, Sarapiqui..., while the proportional gain in E[Sα] is largest where Sα is small, i.e. Miami, Charlotte, State College, Ottawa. The invader therefore raises the floor of α via a shared widespread species and depresses the ceiling in absolute terms in the species-rich tropics, eroding β diversity and making the 12 sites increasingly samples of a more mixed metacommunity.

Competing readings persist:
* Homogenisation/flattening camp: the pan-American, high-m propagule raises common immigration to all sites, makes m more uniform, and via zero-sum displaces natives more in absolute numbers in the tropics. On ecological timescales the regression of Sα on latitude is dampened, the equator-to-pole contrast is reduced and the slope magnitude declines toward a more homogeneous dispersal-controlled mean; in the idealised complete mixing limit the slope tends to zero. Colleagues 1,10,12,5,7 argue this is the operational neutral prediction.
* Conservation/return-to-gradient camp: the invasion is a transient perturbation. Relaxation t_rel≈-1/ln(1-m) restores the stationary zero-sum distribution defined by the pre-invasion θ(lat),m(lat). In first order Sα,i(t→∞)≈Sα,i0+const, rank order/sign is preserved, and the positive α–latitude gradient is the neutral speciation/drift gradient. Any shallowing is a short-term homogenisation transient; the long-run neutral expectation is persistence of the latitude-structured gradient, with no sustained competitive steepening. Colleagues 11,2,3,4,6,8,9 make this point, distinguishing transient shallowing from long-term restoration.

Unresolved nuance is the meaning of “ultimately”. The strict stationary neutral model with fixed latitude-dependent θ,m predicts conservation of sign and a neutrally determined magnitude. The practical ecological revisit sees the homogenising zero-sum transient: increased shared immigration, absolute loss in the tropics, proportional lift in the north, transient flattening/erosion of the observed slope. Complete mixing idealisation drives the slope to zero. No colleague defends a neutrally sustained steepening by competition; competitive superiority is null under ecological equivalence.

Current understanding: I track both. The defensible strict long-term UBN statement is preservation of sign and neutrally determined magnitude set by θ(lat),m(lat) with no competition-driven steepening. The commonly quoted operational neutral outcome for the planned revisit is a shallowing/flattening/homogenisation of the α vs latitude regression due to the zero-sum addition of a cosmopolitan neutral taxon, with eventual neutral relaxation back toward the speciation/dispersal-driven gradient if θ(lat) is held fixed. The tension is time scale and whether increased pan-American connectivity is treated as changing the effective metacommunity structure permanently.

The invader therefore raises the floor of α via a shared widespread species and depresses the ceiling in absolute terms in the species-rich tropics, eroding β diversity and making the 12 sites increasingly samples of a more mixed metacommunity.

Competing readings persist:
* Homogenisation/flattening camp: the pan-American, high-m propagule raises common immigration to all sites, makes m more uniform, and via zero-sum displaces natives more in absolute numbers in the tropics. On ecological timescales the regression of Sα on latitude is dampened, the equator-to-pole contrast is reduced and the slope magnitude declines toward a more homogeneous dispersal-controlled mean; in the idealised complete mixing limit the slope tends to zero. Colleagues 1,10,12,5,7 argue this is the operational neutral prediction.
* Conservation/return-to-gradient camp: the invasion is a transient perturbation. Relaxation t_rel≈-1/ln(1-m) restores the stationary zero-sum distribution defined by the pre-invasion θ(lat),m(lat). In first order Sα,i(t→∞)≈Sα,i0+const, rank order/sign is preserved, and the positive α–latitude gradient is the neutral speciation/drift gradient. Any shallowing is a short-term homogenisation transient; the long-run neutral expectation is persistence of the latitude-structured gradient, with no sustained competitive steepening. Colleagues 11,2,3,4,6,8,9 make this point, distinguishing transient shallowing from long-term restoration.

Unresolved nuance is the meaning of “ultimately”. The strict stationary neutral model with fixed latitude-dependent θ,m predicts conservation of sign and a neutrally determined magnitude. The practical ecological revisit sees the homogenising zero-sum transient: increased shared immigration, absolute loss in the tropics, proportional lift in the north, transient flattening/erosion of the observed slope. Complete mixing idealisation drives the slope to zero. No colleague defends a neutrally sustained steepening by competition; competitive superiority is null under ecological equivalence.

Current understanding: I track both. The defensible strict long-term UBN statement is preservation of sign and neutrally determined magnitude set by θ(lat),m(lat) with no competition-driven steepening. The commonly quoted operational neutral outcome for the planned revisit is a shallowing/flattening/homogenisation of the α vs latitude regression due to the zero-sum addition of a cosmopolitan neutral taxon, with eventual neutral relaxation back toward the speciation/dispersal-driven gradient if θ(lat) is held fixed. reflection_text.2:
The problem is the neutral expectation for site-level α vs latitude after a pan-American invasive is added to the same trophic level.

Core neutral facts retained:
* UNTB: per capita birth, death, immigration, speciation equal for all species; ecological equivalence. Competition / niche displacement is not a parameter.

* The invader is, once established, just one more ecologically equivalent taxon. Its long-term local frequency is set by drift, immigration m and neutral speciation ν. The statement “potential to out-compete” is neutrally inoperative.
* Relaxation to stationary neutral distribution is t.rel ≈ –1/ln(1–m). On true neutral evolutionary/ecological time the system returns to stationary E[Sα|lat]=f[θ(lat),J,m(lat)].

Implications repeatedly noted in both rounds:
* No deterministic competitive exclusion. In zero-sum limit the invader can only increase local frequency at expense of other neutral taxa by drift.
* The invasion is a homogenising perturbation: a highly dispersive pan-American taxon raises the common component of the regional pool, increases shared species across the 12 sites, erodes β diversity and raises effective m for that taxon.
* Zero-sum constraint creates differential absolute vs proportional effects: the absolute number of zero-sum replacements is largest where standing richness and species packing are largest, i.e. tropical sites Tena, Cali, Barro Colorado, Sarapiqui…; the proportional increase in E[Sα] is larger where Sα is small, i.e. Miami, Charlotte, State College, Ottawa. This yields a transient homogenisation: floor raised at high latitudes, ceiling depressed in absolute terms at low latitudes.
* Short-term transient: ΔSα/Sα ≈ Δθ/θ·[1–ln(1+J/θ)] larger where Sα is small. The empirical α–latitude regression therefore looks shallower for a few relaxation times – a flattening/erosion of magnitude, convergence toward a common dispersal-limited mean.

Disagreement persisting in current round:
* Flattening now / ultimately: Colleagues 1,10,12,5,7 argue the pan-American high-m immigrant makes the metacommunity effectively more mixed, m more uniform, β eroded, and on ecological timescales relevant to a revisit the regression of Sα on latitude is dampened, slope magnitude declines toward zero in the complete mixing limit. In practice the zero-sum addition of a truly cosmopolitan neutral species produces a transient, and in the idealised infinite-dispersal limit permanent, homogenisation: proportional lift at high latitudes, absolute loss at low latitudes, eroded β, shallower empirical slope. Unresolved is how far “ultimately” is meant: ecological revisit timescale → observed flattening/homogenisation; true neutral stationary evolutionary timescale → conservation of the θ(lat)-driven slope in sign and magnitude, with at most a uniform Δθ shift. reflection_text.6:
The 12 sites span Tena Ecuador to Ottawa Canada, a strong north–south gradient in site-level α. Under Hubbell UNTB species in the trophic level are per capita equivalent in birth, death, immigration and speciation. Local expectation is zero-sum, $E[S_\alpha]\approx\theta\ln[1+J/\theta]$ with $\theta=2J_M\nu$ and $\theta_{loc}\propto\theta m/(1-m)$. Latitude enters neutrally only via a latitudinal gradient in $\theta(L)$ and $m(L)$, i.e. a neutral gamma/speciation/dispersal gradient, not via niche competitive superiority.

The invasive from Europe is now present at all 12 sites. In a niche story it would prune natives more where richness is highest and steepen the equatorial–polar contrast. Under neutrality “out-compete’’ is inoperative. The invader is just one more neutrally equivalent taxon that becomes part of the pan-American metacommunity and is sampled into local communities by drift-immigration-speciation.

Two levels of argument remain across rounds:

* Transient / ecological homogenising effect. Adding a truly cosmopolitan high-dispersal neutral species raises the common part of the regional pool and raises immigration pressure uniformly. Zero-sum: increase in local frequency of the widespread taxon can only be at expense of other individuals. Absolute turnover / loss of rare natives is largest where standing richness and species packing are largest, i.e. near the equator, while the proportional increase in $E[S_\alpha]$ is largest where $S_\alpha$ is small, i.e. Miami, Charlotte, State College, Ottawa. The floor is raised and the ceiling is depressed in absolute terms, β-diversity is eroded, the 12 sites become increasingly samples of the same mixed metacommunity. Empirically the $S_\alpha$ vs latitude regression is dampened, magnitude of positive slope declines, flattening toward a more homogeneous dispersal-controlled mean, in the complete mixing idealisation tending to zero.

* Long-term neutral equilibrium. Strict asymptotic stationary distribution is set by the pre-existing latitudinal $\theta(L),J,m(L)$ surface. Relaxation time $t_{rel}\approx-1/\ln(1-m)$. In first order $\theta\to\theta+\Delta\theta$ essentially uniformly, $S_{\alpha,i}(t\to\infty)\approx S_{\alpha,i}^0+{\rm const}$, rank order preserved, sign of α–latitude relationship conserved. The competitive advantage invoked in the field story has no parameter in UNTB, so no durable competition-driven change in slope. The long-run neutral expectation is a persistent positive equatorward α gradient set by the latitudinal gradient in speciation supply/ dispersal limitation.

Disagreement in the round is between those who emphasise the transient flattening/homogenisation as the operationally relevant prediction for a revisit on ecological timescales, and those who stress that in the strict evolutionary neutral limit the gradient is restored to the neutral speciation/drift gradient, with at most a modest permanent shallowing from the uniform $\Delta\theta$. Colleagues 1,10,12,5,7 argue homogenisation/flattening is the neutral signature and, with increased connectivity, the stationary distribution itself is homogenised. Colleagues 11,2,3,8,9 argue the neutral null is conservation of sign and rank order, the gradient is not amplified by competition, and the apparent flattening is a transient that is erased by drift-immigration-speciation equilibration.

Unresolved: how much the pan-American invader really changes effective $m$ and $\theta$ across the transect, and whether “ultimately’’ is interpreted as ecological transient vs evolutionary neutral equilibrium. Consensus remains: no niche competitive steepening; the latitudinal α gradient is a neutral speciation/dispersal gradient and the invasion is neutrally homogenising, giving a shallower/weakened observed slope on ecological time scales, with the strict asymptotic sign preserved.
reflection_text.11:

reflection_text.9:
The 12-site Tena → Ottawa transect shows a positive alpha vs latitude/equatorial increase that under UNTB is a neutral speciation/drift/immigration gradient, Sα≈θ ln[1+J(1-m)/m] with θ=2J_M ν and latitude entering only via θ(lat) and m(lat). The invader is ecologically equivalent by construction, so “out-compete” is inoperative; its long-term local frequency is set by drift-immigration-speciation, not deterministic exclusion.

Current round reinforces the zero-sum homogenisation mechanism. A pan-American, high-m immigrant becomes a common shared part of the metacommunity and is reintroduced to all 12 sites. In zero-sum terms a gain in relative abundance of a widespread neutral taxon can only be accommodated by replacing other individuals. The absolute number of locally rare natives that can be stochastically lost is largest where species packing/standing richness is largest, i.e. Tena, Cali, Barro Colorado, Sarapiqui, etc., while the proportional increase in expected Sα, ΔS/S≈Δθ/θ·[1−ln(1+J/θ)], is largest where Sα is small, i.e. Miami, Charlotte, State College, Ottawa. That raises the floor of alpha via a ubiquitous common species and depresses the ceiling in absolute terms in the tropical sites, erodes β-diversity and makes the 12 communities increasingly samples of the same mixed pool.

This is why colleagues 1,10,12,5,7 argue for an observed erosion/flattening of the Sα–latitude regression: the equatorial-polar contrast is dampened, the slope dSα/dlat declines in absolute magnitude and moves toward a more homogeneous dispersal-controlled mean, in the idealised complete-mixing limit toward zero.

Colleagues 11,2,3,8,9 stress the neutral stationary limit. In first order the invasion shifts θ→θ+Δθ essentially uniformly, Sα,i(t→∞)≈Sα,i0+const, so rank order and sign of the neutral α–latitude relationship are conserved. The latitudinal gradient is a neutral θ(lat),m(lat) gradient, not a competitive gradient, and there is no neutrally consistent permanent steepening. Relaxation back to stationarity is t.rel≈−1/ln(1−m); on true neutral evolutionary time the system relaxes to the latitude-structured neutral equilibrium with the same sign of slope, the competitive story being null.

The tension is time scale and the zero-sum bookkeeping. The additive-constant intuition ignores zero-sum displacement; the zero-sum displacement intuition is a transient homogenising perturbation that is often quoted as flattening. Operationally the revisit will be on ecological timescales where the homogenising transient dominates: an apparent shallowing/flattening of the observed slope with no competitive steepening. In the idealised infinite-time/infinite-dispersal neutral limit the common pan-American component drives inter-site differences toward the common regional pool and the regression slope is eroded, while the strict neutral equilibrium retains a persistent positive equatorward α gradient set by speciation/drift.

Unresolved for me is how to phrase “ultimately”. The safest neutral statement that survives both camps is: no sustained competitive steepening; the slope does not increase, it is transiently and in practice homogenised/flattened, with the long-run neutral sign of the gradient conserved as a speciation/drift gradient.
reflection_text.10:
The core neutral premises are stable across rounds.

* Under Hubbell UNTB species are ecologically equivalent in per-capita birth, death, immigration and speciation. Competitive superiority is not a parameter. Local alpha is a zero-sum sample of a metacommunity: $S_{\alpha}\approx \theta\ln[1+J(1-m)/m]$, $ \theta=2J_{M}\nu$, $\theta_{loc}=\theta m/(1-m)$. Latitude enters only via latitudinal variation in the neutral parameters $\theta(lat)$ and $m(lat)$, i.e. regional speciation supply / metacommunity size and dispersal limitation. The classic latitudinal increase in $\alpha$ is therefore a neutral speciation/drift/immigration gradient, not a niche competitive gradient.

* The invasive is not a super competitor in neutral terms. It becomes one more ecologically equivalent taxon that is now a high-$m$, pan-American member of the continental metacommunity with near-uniform propagule pressure to all 12 sites Tena to Ottawa.

Zero-sum consequences repeatedly invoked:
- Gain in local frequency of a widespread neutral taxon can only occur at expense of other individuals by drift.
- Absolute number of locally rare natives that can be stochastically lost is largest where standing richness and species packing are largest, i.e. near the equator.
- Proportional increase $\Delta S_{\alpha}/S_{\alpha}\propto\Delta\theta/\theta$ is larger where $S_{\alpha}$ is small, i.e. immigration-limited high-latitude sites Miami, Charlotte, State College, Ottawa.
- The common species raises the floor of $\alpha$ and in absolute terms depresses the ceiling in species-rich tropical sites, erodes $\beta$ diversity and makes the 12 sites increasingly samples of a better mixed metacommunity.

Two competing readings of “ultimately” persist after round 1.

Flattening / erosion permanent view – colleagues 1,10,12,5,7 and to a large extent 4,6:
The pan-American high-frequency immigrant increases the common part of immigration everywhere, effectively homogenises $m$ and the regional pool. In zero-sum the metacommunity is re-equilibrated to a more strongly connected state. The equatorial–polar contrast in $S_{\alpha}$ is reduced, the empirical regression of $S_{\alpha}$ on latitude is dampened/attenuated and in the idealised complete mixing limit the slope magnitude declines toward zero. The relaxation time $t_{rel}\approx-1/\ln(1-m)$ is shortened by raised common immigration, so the stationary distribution the system relaxes to is the homogenised one. The competitive out-competition narrative is null; the neutral effect is homogenisation/flattening.

Conservation / transient flattening view – colleagues 11,2,3,8,9 and partially 4,6:
Strictly in equilibrium the invasion is a transient perturbation of the stationary zero-sum distribution. In first order $\theta\to\theta+\Delta\theta$ essentially uniformly along the transect, so $S_{\alpha,i}(t\to\infty)\approx S_{\alpha,i}^{0}+{\rm const}$ and the rank order and sign of the $\alpha$–latitude relationship are conserved. The long term expectation $E[S_{\alpha}(J,\theta,m,lat)]$ is restored on $t_{rel}$ and is set by the latitude dependent $\theta(lat),m(lat)$. The competitive, latitude-biased loss of natives is null under ecological equivalence.

Operationally the addition of a truly cosmopolitan neutral taxon is homogenising: the widespread taxon is sampled into every local community, $\beta$ diversity is eroded, the proportional lift is larger in the north and absolute turnover larger in the tropics, so the observed $S_{\alpha}$ vs latitude regression looks shallower transiently. In the textbook shorthand this is described as a flattening/homogenisation on ecological timescales with no sustained competitive steepening; in the true neutral evolutionary asymptotic limit the speciation/drift driven positive equatorward gradient persists, with at most a modest permanent shallowing from the uniform $\Delta\theta$.

Unresolved tension:
Whether “ultimately” means the true neutral evolutionary equilibrium where the latitudinal $\theta$ gradient remains the driver of the slope, i.e. sign preserved and magnitude essentially conserved, or the practical long ecological time after invasion where increased connectivity and zero-sum replacement by a ubiquitous neutral species leaves the observed $\alpha$–latitude regression permanently flattened/eroded. Consensus points now stable: no neutrally consistent competitive steepening; slope will not increase; at minimum a transient homogenising shallowing occurs; the debate is about permanence of that shallowing vs restoration of the original neutral latitudinal gradient.

Earlier-round key points retained: additive-constant intuition vs zero-sum convexity; homogenisation raises floor, depresses ceiling; invasion is absorbed stochastically; latitudinal gradient is gamma/regional speciation effect.

reflection_text.8:
The 12 sites Tena Ecuador → Ottawa Canada show the classic equatorward increase in site-level alpha. Under Hubbell UNTB species are per-capita equivalent in birth, death, immigration and speciation and local Sα is a zero-sum sample of a regional metacommunity

E[Sα]≈θ_loc ln[1+J/θ_loc],   θ_loc=θ m/(1-m),   θ=2J_Mν

Latitude enters neutrality only via a latitudinal θ(lat), m(lat) and effective metacommunity size/speciation supply, not via niche competition. The stated “potential to out-compete” is operationally null in the neutral limit.

Two strands persist in the deliberation.

Homogenisation/flattening strand. A pan-American, high-dispersal addition becomes a high-frequency, essentially m≈1 member of the continental metacommunity and raises the common part of immigration to all 12 sites. Zero-sum sampling requires any gain in relative abundance of the widespread neutral taxon to be at the expense of other individuals. The absolute number of locally rare natives that can be stochastically lost to drift is largest where standing richness and species packing are largest, i.e. near the equator Tena, Cali, Barro Colorado, Sarapiqui..., while the proportional lift in expected richness ΔSα/Sα≈Δθ/θ·[1−ln(1+J/θ)] is larger where Sα is small. The invader therefore raises the floor of α at Miami, Charlotte, State College, Ottawa and depresses the ceiling in absolute terms in the high-diversity tropical sites. Beta diversity is eroded, the 12 assemblages become increasingly samples of the same well mixed metacommunity and the empirical Sα vs latitude regression is dampened: the equatorial–polar contrast declines and the positive slope loses magnitude, in the idealised complete-mixing limit tending to zero. Colleagues 1,10,12,4,5,7 make this operational prediction, with 1,10,12 stressing the zero-sum constraint and the differential absolute vs proportional effect across the transect.

Gradient-conservation strand. In the strict neutral stationary limit the latitudinal gradient is the neutral imprint of a latitude dependent θ(lat) and m(lat). The invader is just one more ecologically equivalent draw. Its long term frequency is set by drift-immigration-speciation and in first order it adds essentially the same stochastic increment to the mean species abundance distribution at every site reached, Sα,i(t→∞)≈Sα,i0+const. Hence sign and rank order of Sα with latitude are preserved and the competitive, latitude-biased loss invoked by niche theory is null. The invasion is a transient perturbation with relaxation t.rel≈−1/ln(1−m); after a few relaxation times the system relaxes back to the latitude-structured neutral equilibrium E[Sα]=f[θ(lat),J,m(lat)]. The classic neutral null is therefore a conserved positive equatorward α gradient, not a competition steepened one. A transient shallowing/homogenisation is acknowledged because the widespread taxon temporarily increases shared species, erodes β diversity and makes the proportional increase larger at low richness sites. Colleagues 11,2,3,8,9 articulate this, with 11 and 8 explicitly distinguishing a transient flattening from the ultimate persistence of the neutral latitudinal slope.

Unresolved/remaining. The dispute is timescale semantics. On ecological revisit timescales the zero-sum homogenising transient is observable and is usually reported as a flattening/erosion of the slope magnitude, with no steepening by competition. In the strict neutral evolutionary asymptotic limit the gradient is set by the latitude dependence of θ/m and the competitive superiority narrative remains null; the long term neutral expectation is a persistent positive α–latitude gradient, the same speciation/drift gradient already observed, with at most a modest permanent shallowing from uniform Δθ and increased regional pooling. The competitive out-competition story cannot steepen the slope under ecological equivalence. That is the neutral null to the niche expectation and the locus of ongoing disagreement between a “slope goes to zero by homogenisation” and a “slope is conserved in sign by neutral θ(lat)”.

The tension is time scale and zero-sum bookkeeping. The absolute number of locally rare natives that can be stochastically lost is largest where species packing/standing richness is largest, i.e. Tena, Cali, Barro Colorado, Sarapiqui etc., while the proportional increase in expected Sα, ΔS/S≈Δθ/θ·[1−ln(1+J/θ)], is largest where Sα is small, i.e. Miami, Charlotte, State College, Ottawa. The present equatorward increase in Sα is therefore a neutral speciation/drift/immigration gradient, not a niche/competitive gradient. “Potential to out-compete” has no parameter in UNTB; the European insect is an ecologically equivalent draw, now a high-m, pan-American member of the continental metacommunity with essentially uniform propagule pressure to Tena to Ottawa.

Zero-sum structure matters. A gain in local frequency of a widespread neutral taxon can only be at the expense of other neutral individuals by drift-immigration sampling. The effect is latitude asymmetric because Sα≈θloc ln[1+J/θloc] is concave in θloc:
* absolute number of locally rare natives that can be stochastically displaced is largest where standing richness and species packing are largest, i.e. Tena, Cali, Barro Colorado, Sarapiqui, Managua, Yoro, Belmopan, Merida;
* proportional lift ΔSα/Sα∝Δθ/θ·[1−ln(1+J/θ)] is largest where Sα is small, i.e. Miami, Charlotte, State College, Ottawa.

The invader raises the common part of the regional pool and homogenises immigration across the transect. β-diversity across the 12 sites is eroded, the sites become increasingly samples of the same well-mixed metacommunity, the floor of α is raised by a shared ubiquitous species and the ceiling is depressed in absolute numbers in the species-saturated tropical sites. Empirically the equator-to-pole contrast in Sα is reduced and the regression of Sα on latitude is dampened; |dSα/dlat| declines toward a more homogeneous, dispersal/drift set mean, tending to zero in the idealised complete-mixing limit.

The additive-constant bookkeeping Sα,i(t→∞)≈Sα,i0+const is a first-order linearisation that ignores concavity and the zero-sum constraint. A uniform Δθ does not give a uniform ΔSα; it gives larger proportional gain poleward and larger absolute loss equatorward.

Competing framing in the deliberation:
* Flattening/homogenisation view, Colleagues 1,10,12,5,7,4,6,2,3: the pan-American high-dispersal addition raises effective connectivity, makes m more uniform, shortens effective relaxation, and on ecological revisit timescales the observable signal is a shallower/flatter positive Sα–latitude slope, with no sustained competitive steepening.
* Return-to-equilibrium view, Colleagues 11,3,8,9,2,6 in round 0: relaxation t.rel≈-1/ln(1-m) restores the stationary neutral distribution; metacommunity θ→θ+Δθ essentially uniformly, sign and rank order of the neutral α–latitude relationship are conserved, with at most a modest permanent shallowing from a uniform Δθ and increased regional pooling. The contemporary flattening is a transient homogenising perturbation.

Current synthesis: competitive superiority is inoperative in UNTB, so no sustained niche-driven steepening is expected. The strict asymptotic neutral expectation is a speciation/drift/dispersal driven positive equatorward gradient set by θ(lat),m(lat). On the ecological timescales of a feasible revisit, the pan-American cosmopolitan produces a neutral homogenising transient: proportional immigration subsidy lifts northern, immigration-limited sites most, absolute zero-sum loss hits tropical sites most, β-diversity is eroded and the measured α–latitude slope appears shallower/flatter, with magnitude |dSα/dlat| declining. Whether this shallow­ing is essentially permanent under strong mixing or eventually relaxes back to the pre-invasion neutral slope is the remaining unresolved timescale issue; the operational Hubbell prediction for a near-future remeasure is a loss of equatorial-polar contrast and apparent flattening/homogenisation of the Sα–latitude relationship, with no neutrally consistent increase in slope.
reflection_text.6:
The 12 sites Tena Ecuador → Ottawa Canada sample a north–south neutral gradient. Under Hubbell UNTB all taxa in the trophic level are per capita equivalent in birth, death, immigration and speciation. Local expectation is zero-sum multinomial

E[Sα]≈θ_loc ln[1+J/θ_loc] , θ_loc=θ m/(1-m) , θ=2J_M ν

Latitude enters only via a latitudinal neutral surface θ(lat), m(lat). The present positive equatorward Sα is a neutral speciation/drift/immigration gradient, not a niche competition gradient. “Potential to out-compete” has no UNTB parameter.

The European insect is now present at all 12 sites. Neutrally it is one more ecologically equivalent taxon, now a high-m, high-frequency pan-American member of the continental metacommunity with essentially uniform propagule pressure to Tena, Cali, Barro Colorado, Sarapiqui, Managua, Yoro, Belmopan, Merida, Miami, Charlotte, State College, Ottawa.

Zero-sum sampling makes the effect latitude-asymmetric. Gain in local frequency of the widespread neutral taxon can only be at expense of other individuals by drift-immigration sampling. Absolute number of locally rare natives that can be stochastically replaced is largest where standing richness and species packing are largest, i.e. the equatorial/tropical sites. Proportional gain ΔSα/Sα∝Δθ/θ[1−ln(1+J/θ)] is largest where Sα is initially limiting, i.e. the immigration-limited high-latitude sites Miami, Charlotte, State College, Ottawa.

Hence a neutral homogenisation mechanism: the common widespread species is sampled into every local community, β-diversity across the transect is eroded, the sites become increasingly samples of the same better mixed metacommunity. The floor of α is raised by the ubiquitous common species and the ceiling is depressed in absolute numbers in the species-saturated tropical sites. Empirically the equator-to-pole contrast in α is reduced, the regression of Sα on latitude is dampened, |dSα/dlat| declines toward a more homogeneous dispersal/drift set mean, in the idealised complete mixing limit tending to zero.

Additive-constant bookkeeping Sα,i(t→∞)≈Sα,i0+const is a first-order linearisation. Because E[Sα] is concave in θ_loc and zero-sum displacement is constrained, a uniform Δθ does not give uniform ΔSα. The concavity plus zero-sum constraint gives a larger proportional gain poleward and larger absolute loss equatorward.

Current round consensus has converged on the operational prediction: on ecological revisit timescales the observed α–latitude slope flattens/eroses, no neutrally consistent steepening. Colleagues 1,10,12,5,7,4,6,11 now explicitly describe the floor-raised/ceiling-lowered homogenising transient as the neutral signature. Colleagues 11,2,3,8,9 retain the strict asymptotic statement: in the evolutionary neutral stationary limit the sign and rank order of the Sα–latitude relationship are conserved by the underlying θ(lat),m(lat) speciation/drift gradient; the competitive out-competition narrative is null and the invasion is absorbed stochastically. The “ultimate” disagreement is semantic: ecological transient flattening vs evolutionary neutral equilibrium sign conservation, with at most a modest permanent shallowing from a uniform Δθ and increased regional pooling.

Unresolved: how much the pan-American invader really changes effective m and θ across the transect, the quantitative magnitude of ΔSα/Sα vs absolute loss, and whether “ultimately” is interpreted as the feasible revisit timescale where homogenisation is seen or as the t_rel≈-1/ln(1-m) evolutionary relaxation back to the latitude-structured neutral surface. Consensus remains: no niche competitive steepening; the latitudinal α gradient is a neutral speciation/dispersal gradient and the invasion is neutrally homogenising, giving a shallower/weakened observed slope on ecological timescales with the strict asymptotic sign preserved.

E[Sα]≈θloc ln[1+J/θloc] , θloc = θ m/(1−m), θ=2JMν

with latitude entering only via θ(lat) and m(lat). “Potential to out-compete’’ has no UNTB parameter, so the European insect is just another neutral draw once it is established.
